questions.prompt: What makes Chapter 11 the tracking story chapter?
choices: It turns tracking into a named organizational case about visible progress and review
It replaces tracking with stretch goals
It argues that reporting alone is enough for accountability

explanation.gentle: The chapter moves tracking out of pure concept and into a named organizational story.
explanation.direct: Its job is to show visible progress and owned correction inside a real case.
explanation.competitive: This story has to prove tracking survives contact with organizational work.

questions.prompt: How does the chapter distinguish real tracking from static reporting?
choices: Real tracking keeps progress visible while teams can still review and adjust
Real tracking waits until the end so the summary is cleaner
Real tracking depends mainly on harsher pressure

explanation.gentle: The chapter values visibility that helps while the work is still alive.
explanation.direct: Tracking matters because it supports review and course correction before the window closes.
explanation.competitive: A late report is softer than a live signal.

questions.prompt: Which common substitute does the chapter reject?
choices: Visible progress
Owned correction
Surveillance or punishment as the main accountability mechanism

explanation.gentle: The chapter says harshness is weaker than clear movement people can review honestly.
explanation.direct: Pressure can imitate seriousness while thinning learning and correction.

questions.prompt: Maya hears that an important goal is receiving updates, but nobody can show what changed in time to guide the next decision. What best fits the chapter?
choices: The team should call the reporting rhythm good enough
The team should identify the visible signs of movement and slippage before the next review
The team should wait for the final result before asking harder questions

explanation.gentle: Updates are weaker than visible progress that can guide action.
explanation.direct: The chapter wants evidence of movement that supports review while correction is still possible.
explanation.competitive: Status rhythm is not proof of motion.

questions.prompt: A yearbook fundraising board discovers the real shortfall only after the deadline is close. What chapter failure does this show?
choices: Healthy accountability through live review
Late reporting that failed to make progress visible soon enough
Too much visible correction too early

explanation.gentle: The problem is not a lack of reports but a lack of timely visibility.
explanation.direct: The chapter separates live tracking from summaries that arrive after leverage fades.
explanation.competitive: Documentation showed up. The signal did not.

questions.prompt: Which misreading does Chapter 11 warn against?
choices: Tracking depends on visible movement and review
Reporting cadence by itself equals tracking
Owned correction matters more than guesswork

explanation.gentle: The chapter warns that a regular update rhythm can still arrive too late to help.
explanation.direct: Reporting cadence is weaker than visibility that changes decisions while the work is live.
explanation.competitive: A schedule of updates is not a schedule of truth.

questions.prompt: What happens when accountability depends mostly on reconstructing progress afterward?
choices: Ownership grows stronger because the story is clearer
Accountability weakens because movement was not visible while it could still be corrected
The chapter says explanation is the best form of review

explanation.gentle: The chapter prefers visible movement over late reconstruction.
explanation.direct: Accountability becomes thinner when people can only explain the work after the useful window closes.
explanation.competitive: Once motion disappears, explanation tries to replace evidence.

questions.prompt: A student service committee wants tougher pressure after progress becomes murky. Which response best fits the chapter?
choices: Add harsher oversight first and visibility later
Drop accountability because pressure feels unfair
Make movement easier to review before confusing seriousness with surveillance

explanation.gentle: Clearer progress signals are stronger than harsher monitoring alone.
explanation.direct: The chapter prefers visible review and course correction over pressure theater.
explanation.competitive: See the work sooner before trying to squeeze people harder.

questions.prompt: What deeper point does the chapter make about visible progress in an organization?
choices: It mainly helps the final report look organized
It turns accountability into evidence-guided ownership because review and correction can happen while the work is still alive
It matters only after the outcome is fixed

explanation.gentle: Visible progress helps people review and respond before the result hardens.
explanation.direct: The chapter makes accountability operational by tying it to live evidence and adjustment.
explanation.competitive: The work becomes harder to bluff when the motion can still answer back.

questions.prompt: Why does Chapter 11 naturally lead into the stretch chapter next?
choices: Because once tracked accountability is visible in a story, the next issue is what happens when goals push beyond safe ambition
Because tracking and accountability no longer matter after this chapter
Because company stories end the argument before new superpowers appear

explanation.gentle: The next step is to ask how visible, owned work changes when the goals become more ambitious.
explanation.direct: Chapter 11 completes the tracking case and hands the book into stretch.
explanation.competitive: After proof of motion comes the question of how far the goal should reach.
